notes: IRobustSerializer serializes the generated state returned for every component instance after load.
This isolates component-state shape and is not a prediction of compressed full-state or packet size.
Both captures passed all hard five-map, depth, teardown, profiler, viewer, and PVS lifecycle gates.

realNetwork.client: Graphical 640x480, 30 FPS limit, null OpenAL backend
realNetwork.milestone: The server diagnostic arms before connection and records transport counters on the first SessionStatus.InGame transition.
notes: Both no-lag processes exited 0 and the client reached InGame.
The later reset brackets a 20-second steady window, but uncontrolled game/timing variation is larger than the component change.
The 100 ms capture configures net.fakelagmin=0.1 and zero random lag on both endpoints.

change.topology: Replicate only the network depth-to-map dictionary. Derive the reverse dictionary and map owner/depth/neighbour fields after client state application and map startup.
change.physics: Keep default immutable bounciness as local prototype data and add one explicit replicated falling boolean to the existing physics state.
change.falling: Keep CMUZFallingComponent as an unsaved server active-set marker; authoritative wake, sleep, stop, and disable paths update CMUZPhysicsComponent.Falling.
change.vehicle: Retain networked component presence while immutable traversal fields produce no generated state. Vehicle support and predicted drift read the explicit falling boolean.
change.behavior: No visibility cap, replication throttle, speculative cache, or transition/prediction policy change was introduced.

fallingPopulation.conclusion: Bush provided no active falling burst, so no marker-churn or burst-volume saving is claimed.

vehicleTraversal.conclusion: The synthetic component proves marker-only generated state; it is not a production vehicle population measurement.

pairedLateJoin.conclusion: One whole-world pair observed a smaller full state, but transport compression/framing produced no byte saving at InGame. No stable packet improvement is claimed.

steadySentByteWindows.conclusion: The ranges overlap and vary more than the state-shape change; the traffic is not attributed to this modernization.

latency100Milliseconds.conclusion: Connection and state application passed with injected delay. The run did not measure latency percentiles or exercise a vehicle edge transition.

validation.releaseBenchmarksBuild: Passed with zero warnings and zero errors.
validation.releaseServerBuild: Passed with zero warnings and zero errors.

focusedIntegrationTests.behavior: Verifies exact five-map client topology on initial connection and reconnect, falling true-to-false state replication without the server marker, and marker-only vehicle defaults.

deferredRisks: Bush had no active falling or vehicle traversal population, so marker-churn and production vehicle late-join savings remain unmeasured.
A real vehicle edge transition, client prediction, correction, and support activation still need a latency capture.
The full-state pair is one uncontrolled whole-world sample; repeated late joins with a controlled world are required before claiming a packet-level improvement.
The 20-second traffic windows contain unrelated game-state traffic and are intentionally not used as an improvement ratio.
The diagnostic logs contain the pre-existing mentor disconnect-handler error during graceful client shutdown; both processes still exited 0 and no client error was recorded.
